statement.p: Compute the line integral of the scalar function f(x,y)= \sqrt{1+9xy}
over the curve y=x^3 for 0\le x \le 7

static.solution:
\mathbf{c}(t)=\left(t, t^3\right) for 0\le t\le 7
[Step 1.] Compute \| {\mathbf{c}}'(t)\|.
We have {\mathbf{c}}'(t)=\frac{\,d}{\,dt}\left\lt t, t^3 \right> = \left\lt 1,3 t^2 \right> \quad\Rightarrow\quad \| {\mathbf{c}}'(t)\| =\sqrt{1+9 t^4} [Step 2.] Write out f\left(\mathbf{c}(t)\right).
We substitute x=t, y= t^3 in f( x,y )=\sqrt{1+9xy} to obtain f\left(\mathbf{c}(t)\right)=\sqrt{1+9t\cdot t^3}=\sqrt{1+9 t^4} [Step 3.] Compute the line integral.
We use the Theorem on Scalar Line Integrals to write \int_{\mathcal{C}} f( x,y ) \,ds = \int_0^{7} f\left(\mathbf{c}(t)\right)\| {\mathbf{c}}'(t)\| \,dt=\int_0^{7} \sqrt{1+9 t^4}\sqrt{1+9 t^4} \,dt= \int_0^{7} \left(1+9 t^4\right) \,dt=t+\frac{9 t^5}{5}\bigg|_0^{7}=\frac{151298}{5}=30259.6
